draft.title: Depreciation
card: Depreciation is the fall in an item's value over time. Here the item loses a fixed percentage of its value each period.
The value is multiplied by the same factor each period. For 15% depreciation the factor is \(1 - 0.15 = 0.85\).
\(A = P(1 - r)^{n}\). \(A\) is the value after \(n\) periods, \(P\) is the starting value, \(n\) is the number of periods and \(r\) is the rate per period as a decimal.
Example: a $20,000 machine loses 10% a year for 3 years. \(A = \$20{,}000 \times 0.9^{3}\), which is \(\$20{,}000 \times 0.729 = \$14{,}580\).
draft.remember: Multiply by \((1 - r)\) once for each period. The value falls, but the rate stays the same.

a.q: A ute costs $50,000 new and depreciates by 10% each year. What is its value after 2 years?
a.why: \(A = \$50{,}000 \times 0.9^{2}\), which is \(\$50{,}000 \times 0.81 = \$40{,}500\). The value $40,000 comes from taking 10% of $50,000 off each year, which ignores that each year's loss is taken from the smaller current value.

b.q: A laptop bought for $2000 depreciates by 20% each year. What is its value after 3 years?
b.why: \(A = \$2000 \times 0.8^{3}\), which is \(\$2000 \times 0.512 = \$1024\). The value $800 comes from taking 20% of the original price off each year, which ignores that each year's loss is taken from the smaller current value.
b.clue: The factor each year is \(1 - 0.20\), used three times.

problems.detail: $40,500 is the only option that is not a round multiple of $5,000. A student could guess that the less-round figure is the compound answer without working it out. A distractor such as $40,050 or $41,000 would remove this cue.
